question.text: Under SEBI PIT Regulations 2015, companies must have a code of conduct for:

answer.text: Prevention of insider trading, including trading windows, pre-clearance procedures, and disclosure requirements for designated persons

explanation.text: The Logic: Under general Indian securities-law practice, listed companies and their designated persons are required to adopt a code of conduct under SEBI's PIT Regulations 2015 framework. The code typically prescribes trading windows (open and closed periods for designated persons), pre-clearance procedures for trades above prescribed thresholds, disclosure obligations for trades by designated persons and their immediate relatives, and reporting of holdings — all aimed specifically at preventing insider trading. The Trap: The PIT code of conduct is not about financial reporting alone, general HR matters like attendance, or only customer complaint handling. It is a specialised insider-trading prevention framework. Note: The detailed listed-company PIT code-of-conduct elements (trading windows, pre-clearance, designated-person disclosures) are not described in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook chapter; this framing reflects general PIT regulatory knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
